# Service Standard Operating Procedure
This procedure applies to the Head of Personnel, Bartenders, Chefs, Botanists, Janitors, Musicians, and the station's entertainers.
## Scope of the Department
Service exists to keep the crew fed, watered, entertained, and working in a clean station. Service work is [italic]not[/italic] optional decoration — a station with no food, no cleaning, and no bar runs measurably worse.
Service personnel [italic]should[/italic] remain reachable in their workplaces rather than wandering the station for the whole shift.
## Food and Drink
Chefs and Bartenders [bold]shall not[/bold] knowingly serve food or drink that will harm the consumer. Adding harmful chemicals, unwanted intoxicants, or non-food substances to crew orders is treated as poisoning under [textlink="Space Law" link="SpaceLaw"].
[italic]A patron asking for something strong is consenting to alcohol. They are not consenting to whatever Chemistry had left over.[/italic]
Novelty and themed dishes are encouraged. Charging crew for basic meals is [bold]not[/bold] permitted; the Bar and Kitchen are station services, not private businesses, unless Command has approved an arrangement.
Service [italic]should[/italic] accommodate dietary needs where the ingredients allow — this includes crew who cannot process standard rations.
## Butchery and Livestock
Station pets and crew-aligned creatures [bold]shall not[/bold] be butchered. This includes the Captain's pet, department mascots, and any creature displaying crew-level intelligence.
Livestock kept for food is fair use. If there is doubt about whether something is livestock or a crewmate, ask Command before reaching for the knife.
## Botany
Botanists [italic]should[/italic] prioritise food crops and medical produce before ornamental or recreational growing.
Growing crops whose primary purpose is intoxication or harm requires approval from the Head of Personnel or Commanding Officer, and the produce [italic]should not[/italic] be distributed to crew who did not ask for it. Anything on the controlled list needs paperwork — see [textlink="Permits" link="GuidePermits"].
Dangerous flora [bold]shall not[/bold] be released into the station. Kudzu and similar aggressive growths are to be contained or destroyed immediately, and Command informed.
## Janitorial
Janitors [italic]should[/italic] prioritise hazards over cosmetics: hull breaches, spilled chemicals, blood, and broken glass in traffic areas come before tidying.
Wet floor signs [italic]should[/italic] be placed and then collected. Leaving a station-wide slip hazard unmarked is a genuine safety failure, not a joke.
Janitors [bold]shall not[/bold] dispose of evidence, bodies, or departmental property without asking the owning department first.
## Entertainment and Disruption
Clowns, Mimes, and Musicians are expected to be disruptive within reason. Disruption stops being acceptable when it prevents another department from doing its job.
[italic]Honking in the halls is the job. Honking in Medical during a resuscitation, or slipping Security mid-arrest, is interference and will be treated as such.[/italic]
Service personnel [bold]shall not[/bold] break into other departments in pursuit of a bit. Access is access.
## Supplies and Restocking
Service [italic]should[/italic] route bulk restock requests through Logistics rather than raiding other departments. See [textlink="Cargo SOP" link="GuideCargoSOP"].
The Head of Personnel is responsible for keeping the department staffed and stocked, and for arbitrating disputes between service workers before they reach Command.
